AXP.rationale: AXP presents a moderately attractive profile anchored by a structurally differentiated closed-loop franchise with elite ROE (33%), robust earnings growth (+17.6% YoY EPS in Q1 2026), and expanding margins (operating margin ~35.9% vs ~33-34% trailing). The P/E has compressed ~18% from its January 2026 peak of 25.2x to 20.7x near its one-year floor, while earnings have accelerated — a favorable disconnect. Fee-based revenue resilience is strong: net card fees hit a record $10B in 2025 (+18% YoY), with 30 consecutive quarters of double-digit card-fee growth. Credit quality remains pristine (2% net charge-offs, 1.1% delinquency as of May 2026). The TheFork acquisition ($700M, announced 2026-06-15) is a strategically coherent catalyst extending the dining ecosystem. However, the score is capped below +0.5 by: (1) a sharp operating cash flow deterioration (-20.2% YoY, -39.0% QoQ) diverging from rising earnings, raising quality-of-earnings questions; (2) rising leverage (debt +14.6% YoY vs equity +8.9%) while OCF declines; (3) yield curve flattening to 0.27% signaling potential credit-cycle headwinds; and (4) intensifying competition from Capital One/Discover's integrated network and JPMorgan's Sapphire Reserve. The verification block flagged a revenue discrepancy ($18.9B vs $10.52B) and net margin discrepancy (15.13% vs 26.6%) between the qual and quant reports — I rely on the quant pack's $10.52B and 26.6% net margin as traceable to the filing, and treat the qual report's figures as using a different accounting basis.
